blood donations are 'gift' transactions that are not easily incorporated into a market-oriented health care sector.
the commercialisation of blood production in New Zealand is not a panacea for the problems of blood supply and quality.
the commercialisation of blood production and distribution has had a detrimental effect on the quality of blood in New Zealand.

the commercialisation of the blood system is not in the interests of New Zealanders.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the New Zealand Blood Service has been successful at maintaining the supply of blood and blood components, and at maintaining the quality of blood products.
blood is a gift, and that the best way to ensure its quality is to keep the system of collection, manufacture and supply as noncommercial as possible.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the current commercialisation of blood production and distribution in New Zealand is a mistake.
the new organisational arrangements for the collection, manufacturing, and distribution of blood products in New Zealand are not working.
